note: Looks, typefaces and marks that a great many generated interfaces share, as this skill's maintainers saw them at the date above. It is a judgement, it dates, and it is yours to change: copy this file into a direction folder as common-looks.json and that copy is used instead. A candidate that sits in one of the looks is said to, not refused; at most one candidate of a study may. A look is matched on what is listed under tests: families (a text or display family), neutrals (warm, cool, neutral), ground (light, dark), ground_colour (saturated, quiet), accent_hue (ranges of hue in degrees, as OKLCH counts them: red near 30, yellow near 100, green near 145, blue near 260, violet near 300), corners (sharp, soft, round), separation (rules, shadow, fill, space), display_class (serif, sans, slab, mono, script), display_width (condensed, normal, wide), display_weight (ranges of weight), labels (sentence, upper), shadow (none, soft, hard). needs is how many of the listed tests have to match. faces are families: one matches a candidate's family of the same name or one that begins with it. marks are found in what a candidate calls its signature (words) and in its signature_css (css); both are regular expressions, read without regard to case.
credit: The looks broadsheet-editorial and flat-colour-and-heavy-type, most of faces, and the ids and subjects of marks restate, in this skill's own words and tests, what the public skill impeccable describes (https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable, Apache-2.0, as it stood at commit b49177d32788f2dc585c42831d845dacf1ebed2c): the paragraph headed Calibration and the list of typefaces in skill/reference/new-work.md, and the entries marked slop in crates/live/assets/antipatterns.json. Nothing of it is copied here, and nothing here runs or needs it.

looks.what: A plain sans, cool greys, a blue-to-violet accent, soft corners and cards lifted by a shadow.
A high-contrast display serif on a warm off-white, with an orange, brown or red accent: the usual answer to a request for something less generic.
A near-black ground with a bright cyan, green or violet accent and a technical or monospaced face: the usual answer to a request for something that looks technical.
A display serif, hairlines between everything, square corners and small labels in spaced capitals: the newspaper or the journal, as the usual answer to a request for something with taste.
A ground of one flat strong colour, very heavy condensed display type, square corners and shadows with a hard edge: the loud poster, as the usual answer to a request for something bold.

marks.what: a small label set above each heading
a grid of lines drawn as a background
a soft halo of colour behind a section
a thick bar of colour down one side of a box
plain shapes standing where a picture should be
an icon in a rounded tile above each heading
something that pulses, blinks or scrolls by itself without end
